authorization-matrix.evidence: `POST /case` returns fictional viewer, editor, and admin identities plus the intended policy.
authorization-matrix.observation: Fifteen fixed requests cover three roles, three primary methods, and two archive paths; vulnerable routes trust interface hiding instead.

checkpoint.question: Why include both admin and ops archive paths?
choices: Alternate paths may reach the same privileged action and need the same policy.
A different URL always implies a public action.
checkpoint.explanation: Authorization attaches to the protected action, not merely one spelling of its URL.

authorization-matrix.findingPrompt: Summarize the role, method, and alternate-path authorization gap.
authorization-matrix.evidencePrompt: Cite vulnerable low-role success and the complete fixed matrix.
authorization-matrix.impactPrompt: Describe report read, edit, delete, and archive impact by role.
authorization-matrix.confidencePrompt: Choose confidence based on complete positive and negative matrix coverage.
authorization-matrix.remediationPrompt: Recommend one central server-side role policy for all route aliases.

deny-default-proof.evidence: The fixed service has an explicit allow matrix and rejects every unlisted method/path combination.
deny-default-proof.observation: Intended operations return 200; disallowed role combinations and unlisted routes return 403; unauthenticated access returns 401.

checkpoint.question: What does deny by default mean here?
choices: Unknown operations are allowed until documented.
Only explicitly allowed role-operation combinations succeed.
checkpoint.explanation: A missing policy entry is a denial, including for alternate or newly added routes.

deny-default-proof.findingPrompt: State how the fixed service handles absent policy rules.
deny-default-proof.evidencePrompt: Cite allowed, role-denied, unauthenticated, and unlisted cases.
deny-default-proof.impactPrompt: Explain how least privilege is preserved without blocking intended work.
deny-default-proof.confidencePrompt: Bound confidence to the tested synthetic matrix.
deny-default-proof.remediationPrompt: Name central policy, server enforcement, alias coverage, default denial, and regression tests.
